articles.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
articles.summary: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.
articles.content:
In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass.

Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him.

More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends.

Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with. But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward.

"He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma.
articles.reasoning: The story highlights efforts to improve the welfare of a traumatized rescued gorilla by finding him a companion, which represents a meaningful positive impact on animal welfare and rehabilitation. It focuses on a single topic with sufficient context about Jojo's background, current situation, and ongoing efforts, and it has broader significance for conservation and animal care communities.
articles.personality_title: Jojo the gorilla seeks a friend after years alone in captivity
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Jojo is a gorilla who was taken from the wild as a baby after his family was killed by poachers. He spent most of his early life in a small cage at a private zoo in Gabon.

**What happened** – Now 11 years old, Jojo lives at the Lekedi Foundation sanctuary but has no gorilla companions. His caretakers want to find him a friend, possibly another rescued or zoo-born gorilla, to help him form bonds and improve his life.

**Impact** – Jojo’s story is important because it shows how long isolation can affect animals like gorillas. Experts say Jojo has faced one of the most extreme cases of loneliness seen in great apes. Finding him a friend could help him recover from trauma and improve his wellbeing.

**What's next step** – The sanctuary and researchers are working carefully to find a suitable companion for Jojo. This process involves understanding his behavior and making sure any new gorilla will be a good match.

**One-sentence takeaway** – After years alone, Jojo the gorilla may soon find a friend to help him heal and live a happier life.
articles.personality_title_fr: Jojo le gorille cherche un compagnon après des années de solitude en captivité
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Jojo est un gorille qui a été capturé bébé après que sa famille ait été tuée par des braconniers. Il a passé la majeure partie de sa jeunesse dans une petite cage dans un zoo privé au Gabon.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Aujourd'hui âgé de 11 ans, Jojo vit dans un sanctuaire nommé Lekedi, mais il n'a pas de compagnons gorilles. Ses soigneurs veulent lui trouver un ami, peut-être un gorille sauvé ou né en captivité, pour qu'il puisse créer des liens et améliorer sa vie.

**Impact** – L'histoire de Jojo est importante car elle montre comment une longue période d'isolement peut affecter les animaux comme les gorilles. Les experts disent que Jojo est probablement l'un des cas les plus extrêmes de solitude chez les grands singes. Trouver un compagnon pourrait l'aider à guérir de son traumatisme et à aller mieux.

**Prochaine étape** – Le sanctuaire et les chercheurs travaillent avec soin pour trouver un compagnon adapté à Jojo. Cela demande de bien comprendre son comportement et de s'assurer que le nouveau gorille sera compatible.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Après des années de solitude, Jojo le gorille pourrait bientôt trouver un ami pour l'aider à guérir et vivre plus heureux.
articles.personality_title_es: Jojo el gorila busca un amigo tras años solo en cautiverio
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Jojo es un gorila que fue capturado cuando era un bebé después de que su familia fuera asesinada por cazadores furtivos. Pasó la mayor parte de su infancia en una pequeña jaula en un zoológico privado en Gabón.

**Qué pasó** – Ahora con 11 años, Jojo vive en un santuario llamado Lekedi, pero no tiene compañeros gorilas. Sus cuidadores quieren encontrarle un amigo, posiblemente otro gorila rescatado o nacido en cautiverio, para que pueda formar vínculos y mejorar su vida.

**Impacto** – La historia de Jojo es importante porque muestra cómo el aislamiento prolongado puede afectar a animales como los gorilas. Los expertos dicen que Jojo es probablemente uno de los casos más extremos de soledad en grandes simios. Encontrar un amigo podría ayudarlo a recuperarse del trauma y mejorar su bienestar.

**Próximo paso** – El santuario y los investigadores están trabajando con cuidado para encontrar un compañero adecuado para Jojo. Esto implica entender su comportamiento y asegurarse de que el nuevo gorila sea compatible.

**Resumen en una frase** – Después de años solo, Jojo el gorila podría pronto encontrar un amigo que lo ayude a sanar y vivir una vida más feliz.
